experiments.title: Study of D/A Conversion Using Binary Weighted Resistor And Measurement Of Its  Resolution

blocks.text: To study 8 bit Digital to Analog Conversion using Binary Weighted Resistors Method and measures its resolution.

Digital to Analog Conversion involve conversion of Digital signal to Analog signal. It is an integral part of any A/D converter. This can be easily accomplished by designing  a resistive network that will change each digital level into an equivalent  binary weighted voltage. There are two methods by which we can do this process. First method is using binary weighted resistor method. In this method the binary coded decimal code is used for the representation of the decimal number. The LSB which is at right most location is expressed as (1 or 0)*2^0, the next bit is 1 or 0*21 and so on, where 0 indicates 0V and 1 indicates 5V). Thus the weight of each column from right to left in n bit converter are 1,2,4,8………2n-1.

Following criteria can be applied to this divider. 
* There must be one input resistor for each digital bit. 
* Beginning with the LSB, each following resistor value is one half of the size of the previous resistor. 
* The full scale output voltage is equal to the positive voltage of the digital I/P signal. 
* The LSB has a weight of 1/ (2n-1),where n is the number of input bits. 
* The change in output voltage due change in LSB is equal to the V/ (2n-1), where V is the digital input voltage level. 
* The output voltage can be found for any digital input signal by using the following modified form of Mill man’s
   theorem. (Image-1&2).
RESOLUTION:- 
Resolution indicates the smallest increment of the output corresponding to a 1 LSB input 
code change. For example for 8 bit DAC, 28= 256 codes, so the resolution is 1/256 of the 
output range.

Connect the trainer kit with its power supply :-
* Give the desired logic input to the 8 BIT BINARY WEIGHTED DACfrom on board slider switches as shown below in
   FIGURE-1.1 
* Measure the equivalent output voltage at VOUT of 8 BIT BINARY WEIGHTED DAC for different digital input voltage 
   level with the help of DMM. 
* Observed the calculated and observed readings for different input levels.

RESOLUTION:- 
Resolution of 8 bit converter can be calculated by using formula 
= (1/2N) ×Vref=0.019V 
Calculated Value of Resolution= (1/28) ×5=0.019V 
For observed value subtract any consecutive observed reading like 0.042-0.021=0.021V, this will give observed Value of Resolution.

* DMM
The analog output voltage can be found for any digital input signal by using the binary weighted resister network and its resolution for 8 bits  is 0.019V(LSB).

experiments.title: Study of D/A conversion using R/2R ladder type method and measurement of its  resolution

blocks.text: To study 8 bit Digital to Analog Conversion using R/2R Ladder type Method and measure its resolution.

Binary R/2R Ladder is a resistive network whose output voltage is properly weighted sum of the Digital input.  

It is constructed of resistors that have only two values. We can see from the FIGURE-2.1 that total resistance looking from any node back towards the terminating resistor or out towards the digital input is 2R. We can use the resistance characteristics of the ladder to determine the output voltage for the various digital inputs. Ladder is composed of linear resistors, it is a linear network and the principle of superposition can be used. This means that the output voltage due to combination of input digital level can be found by simply taking the sum of the output levels caused by each digital input individually. To keep the ladder in perfect balance and to maintain symmetry, the output of ladder should be terminated in a resistance of 2R.This will result in lowering of output voltage, but if the 2R load is maintained constant, the output voltage will still be a properly weighted sum of binary input bits. If load is varied, the output voltage will not be a properly weighted sum hence load should be kept constant.

1) Connect the trainer kit with its power supply. 
2) Give the desired logic input to the converter from on board slider switches  of 8 BIT R/2R LADDER  DAC SECTION   
     as shown below in FIGURE-2.1 
3) Measure the equivalent output voltage for different digital input voltage level with the help of DMM at VOUT of 8   
     BIT R/2R LADDER DAC. 
4) Observed the calculated and observed readings for different input levels.

RESOLUTION 
Resolution of 8 bit converter can be calculated by  
Formula = (1/2N) ×Vref=0.019V 
Calculated Value of Resolution= (1/28) ×5=0.019V. 
For observed value subtract any consecutive observed reading like 0.0388
0.0186=0.020V.This will give observed Value of Resolution.

experiments.title: D/A conversion using monolithic IC DAC0800 &to measure    its settling time & effect of settling time.

blocks.text:
To study 8 bit Digital to Analog Conversion using Monolithic IC DAC0800 for various digital data pattern and to measure 
a) Ramp in unipolar and bipolar configuration 
b) Settling time 
c) Effect of settling time on DAC0800.

The DAC0800 series are monolithic 8-bit high-speed current–output digital-to-analog converters (DAC) featuring typical settling time of 100ns.when used as a multiplying DAC monotonic performance over a 40 to 1 reference current range is possible. The DAC0800 are also features high compliance complementary current output to allow differential output voltage of 20V p-p with simple resistor load. The noise immune inputs of the DAC0800 series will accept TTL level with the logic threshold pin, VLC, grounded. Changing the VLC potential will allow direct interface to other logic families. The performance and characteristics of the device are essentially unchanged over the full ±4.5 to ±18 V power supply range; power dissipation is only 33Mw with ±5V supplies and is independent of the logic input states. 
FEATURES OF DAC0800
* Full scale error: ±1LSB 
* Nonlinearity over temperature: ±0.1% 
* Full scale current drift: ±10 ppm/0c 
* High output compliance: -10 V to 18V
* Complementary current output 
* Interface directly with TTL, CMOS, PMOS and others 
* 2 quadrant wide range multiplying capability 
* Wide power supply range:±4.5V to ±18V 
* Low power consumption: 33mW at ±5V 
* Low cost 
* Fast Settling output Current: 100ns
SETTLING TIME 
The settling time of a DAC is the time from a change of digital code to when the output comes within and remains within some error band as shown in Figure below  with  the error band will almost invariably be ± 1 or ± 1/2 LSB.  
The settling time of a DAC is made up of four different periods: the switching time or dead time (during which the digital switching, but not the output, is changing), the slewing time (during which the rate of change of output is limited by the slew rate of the DAC output), the recovery time (when the DAC is recovering from its fast slew and may overshoot), and the linear settling time (when the DAC output approaches its final value in an exponential or near-exponential manner). If the slew time is short compared to the other three (as is usually the case with current output DACs), the settling time will be largely independent of the output step size. On the other hand, if the slew time is a significant part of the total, the larger the step, the longer the settling time. (FIGURE-3.1)
EFFECT OF SETTLING TIME 
The importance of settling time in a data conversion system is that certain analog operations must be performed in sequence, and one operation may be accurately settled before the next operation can be initiated. In DACs this parameter gives information about the time required by the converter to meet the right output value after a change in the input code. Less settling time results in fast conversion and consumes less time than more settling time.

SETTLING TIME MEASUREMENT 
PROCEDURE:- 
1. To measure the settling time, give TTL square wave of 1 KHz from Function generator to all the input (B1-B8) of
     the 8 BIT MONOLITHIC DAC by shorting all the input together as shown in FIGURE-3.8 
2. Observe the transition at VOUT of the 8 BIT MONOLITHIC DAC and measure the time required to change from 
     output high to output low state. This will give the fall time of DAC0800 shown in FIGURE-3.11 
3. The time required to change from O/P low to O/P high will give the Rise time of DAC 0800. Measure the Rise time  
     as shown in FIGURE-3.10 
4. These two readings will give the settling time of whole system i.e. DAC 0800 and LM741.

Frequency -54K Hz. 
At this frequency ON-TIME of input signal is equal to the RISE-TIME of output waveform. Hence we are getting a triangular waveform. Since fall time of output is less than off time of input we are getting some flatness in lower edge of output signal as shown in FIGURE 3.13.

DAC0800 is used for digital to analog conversion in unipolar as well as bipolar mode and output voltage depends on the applied digital input voltage and should not exceed the applied reference voltage. Settling time can be observed from the DSO at different input frequency.
